title.narrative: One Health Companion Animal Program in Nauru 2023-2024 and 2024-2025

description.narrative: DFAT funds Darwin-based NGO Animal Management in Rural and Remote Indigenous Communities to lead a One Health / companion animal program in Nauru. This program consists of three to four visits annually to Nauru by veterinary science teams. Their primary focus is the provision of veterinary services to Nauruan dogs and cats (for which there is no domestic capacity) including surgery, desexing, medication, etc. They also provide education (including in schools) on dog safety, consult to the Government of Nauru, and undertake surveillance of zoonotic diseases.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: INNO658 One Health Companion Animal Program is delivered by the NGO AMRRIC (Animal Management in Rural and Remote indigenous Communities). AMRRIC are based out of Darwin and their primary focus is animal management in remote and rural Indigenous communities in the Northern Territory, but they were commis-sioned by Nauru Post to undertake an animal management program in Nauru after growing issues with the stray dog population. This is their first program in the Pacific but the cultural competencies from the NT have served them well at stakeholder engagement here. Each year, they send four teams of vets each year and in the last 12 months have provided clinical care or antiparasitic treatment to 538 animals, in-cluding 106 desexing surgeries. They also delivered a school-based animal health education program and have delivered lessons on 'Staying Safe around Dogs’ to 756 students in Years 11-5. They assist Government of Nauru with policy development around animal management, quarantine, and One Health. The program relies on volunteer vets which keeps costs low and is one of the most popular programs that Australia runs among the Nauruan community with huge public diplomacy out-comes.
